title: BNCI 2015-006 Music BCI dataset
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 11 healthy participants performing a multi-streamed musical oddball task designed to investigate auditory attention and brain-computer interface applications. Participants selectively attended to one of three concurrent instruments in polyphonic music clips while detecting deviant patterns, with EEG signals recorded at 64 channels and preprocessed to 250 Hz sampling rate. The study demonstrates that attended instruments can be classified from ongoing EEG with 91% mean accuracy using linear discriminant analysis, establishing polyphonic music as a novel and ecologically valid stimulus modality for auditory BCI research.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired from 64 active electrodes (Brain Products actiCAP, 10-10 montage) at 1000 Hz with left mastoid reference. Participants listened to 40-second polyphonic music clips containing three concurrent instruments (Synth-Pop or Jazz conditions) with embedded standard and deviant patterns. Preprocessing included downsampling to 250 Hz, Chebyshev lowpass filtering (42 Hz passband), epoching (-200 to 1200 ms), baseline correction, and artifact rejection (100 μV threshold on Fp1/Fp2). Classification used linear discriminant analysis with shrinkage covariance on spatio-temporal features, evaluated via leave-one-clip-out cross-validation.
